studies.label: Main experiment: collaborative alternate uses with ChatGPT-4, followed by unaided immediate and three-week retention post-tests

counts_source.quote: The valid sample consisted of 52 dyads/104 participants, with 26 dyads/52 participants per experimental condition.

arms.name: Experimental AI group
arms.description: Self-formed dyads randomly assigned to off-the-shelf ChatGPT-4 in a chat window during the main AUT; free prompting, no researcher pre-prompting, and no copy-pasting into the answer box. AI was removed for both post-tests (PDF pp. 4-6, Sections 3 and 4.2).

arms.name: Control non-AI group
arms.description: Dyads randomly assigned to the same AUT and interface without AI; both post-tests were also unaided (PDF pp. 5-6, Sections 4.2.2-4.2.4).

studies.task: Computer Science students produced alternate uses for fork, flower pot, and suitcase as dyads, then for a glass bottle in an immediate unaided dyad post-test, and for key, brick, and gymnastics ball individually in an unaided online retention test three weeks later (PDF pp. 5-6, Section 4.2).

ai_tool.name: ChatGPT-4
ai_tool.locator: PDF p. 4, Section 3; PDF p. 5, Section 4.2.2. Model release year is not stated. Reference [80] on PDF p. 16 gives a March 2024 version of gpt-4 but is cited for ChatGPT in general on PDF p. 1; the Methods do not confirm that version.

preregistration.where: AsPredicted, https://aspredicted.org/msym-tbc2.pdf (PDF p. 4, Section 3; PDF pp. 13-14, Section 6.4). The paper specifies preregistered hypotheses for flexibility and originality in each test phase, but does not explicitly designate primary outcomes. The registration could not be retrieved in this extraction.

not_extracted.what: S2 pre-study: AI-only chatbots versus human dyads, including AUT elaboration (S2-O1) and originality (S2-O2)
not_extracted.reason: No people were randomized to AI assistance: the chatbots worked alone and their answers were compared with human dyads. This is ai_vs_human context, outside Phase 2 extraction (PDF p. 4, Section 4.1). The pre-study was published separately as reference [7] (PDF p. 15).

not_extracted.what: S1 main-test fluency: top-quartile AI versus control comparison
not_extracted.reason: Subgroup comparison of high performers, not the full randomized sample. Its means and SD statement cannot replace full-sample values (PDF p. 8, Section 5.1.1).

not_extracted.what: S1 main-test flexibility: top-quartile AI versus control comparison
not_extracted.reason: Subgroup comparison of high performers, not the full randomized sample. Its means and SD statement cannot replace full-sample values (PDF p. 8, Section 5.1.1).

not_extracted.what: S1 perception-of-AI questionnaires, perceived AI roles and helpfulness, self-assessed ability to generate the AI answers, intended future AI use, and interim AI-use questionnaire
not_extracted.reason: Self-reports, attitudes, intentions, or AI-use reports rather than creativity scored on produced task output. The interim questionnaire is described without reported results (PDF p. 6, Sections 4.2.4 and 4.4.2; PDF p. 10, Section 5.2 and Figure 13).

not_extracted.what: S1 prompt specificity scores and prompt-type counts
not_extracted.reason: Process measures of how the AI group prompted ChatGPT, not creativity scores on AUT output and not a randomized between-arm comparison (PDF pp. 7-8, Section 4.5.4 and Table 1; PDF pp. 11-12, Section 5.3 and Tables 3-4).

not_extracted.what: S1 human-AI interaction patterns, timing of AI use, generation time, and reported collaboration strategies
not_extracted.reason: Process and self-report analyses, without a randomized contrast on the creativity of task output (PDF pp. 7-8, Section 4.5.4 and Table 2; PDF pp. 10-11, Section 5.3).

not_extracted.what: S1 handling of AI-generated answers and human/AI contributions to entered AUT answers
not_extracted.reason: Table 5 reports AI-arm-only process counts and proportions, with no corresponding control contrast. Its entered-answer total is not substituted for the scored main-test fluency mean in Figure 4 (PDF pp. 11-12, Section 5.3 and Table 5).

not_extracted.what: S1 AI-answer acceptance-rate association with main-test fluency
not_extracted.reason: Spearman correlation within the AI arm, not a randomized AI-versus-comparison effect. Its uncertainty also has an unresolved inconsistency with the dyad label (PDF p. 11, Section 5.3 and Figure 14).

not_extracted.what: S1 prompt-specificity associations with AUT dimensions
not_extracted.reason: Within-AI-arm process correlations, not randomized configuration contrasts; the text reports no correlations without numerical test results (PDF p. 11, Section 5.3).

not_extracted.what: S1 demographic and prior private AI-use group differences and associated correlation/moderation checks
not_extracted.reason: Baseline characteristics and confounding/moderation checks are not eligible full-sample contrasts on scored creative output (PDF p. 6, Section 4.3).

open_items: The paper refers to Supplementary Materials, but none were on file or embedded in the PDF. Detailed scoring, sample/bias analyses, questionnaires, and interaction examples are described as supplementary; additional outcome-statistic coverage is unknown (PDF pp. 5-7 and 10).

Initial randomized counts and numbers excluded by the German-language criterion are not printed. The reported valid-sample counts are used for the main and immediate tests; clusters_per_arm describes analyzed dyads, not a confirmed pre-exclusion randomization total (PDF p. 5, Section 4.2.1; PDF p. 6, Section 4.3).

The elaboration Mann-Whitney U values in the main and immediate post-tests cannot be reconciled with an ordinary comparison using the stated dyads per arm. The paper does not establish the actual test rows or a correction for within-dyad dependence. Dyad-level inference and analysis files are needed; no inferential sample size is reconstructed from U or p (PDF pp. 8-9, Sections 5.1.1-5.1.2).

Retention was performed individually, but Figure 12 labels dyads while Figure 1 depicts individuals. Analyzed retention counts, attrition, and the level of aggregation are not confirmed, so retention n_treatment, n_control, n_total, and n_units are null (PDF pp. 5-6, Sections 4.2 and 4.2.4; PDF p. 10, Figure 12).

Only immediate post-test fluency has full-sample arm means and SDs in the narrative. Other arm levels occur only in raster figures and are not transcribed under extraction rule 1. Remaining SDs, SEs, CIs, effect sizes, and nonsignificant test statistics are not printed in the available text/tables (PDF pp. 8-10, Section 5.1 and Figures 4-12).

Immediate fluency SDs describe collaborative dyad scores; the exact computational rows are not explicitly identified, and the allowed sd_level vocabulary has no team value. sd_level remains null rather than assigning these SDs to people or individual ideas. No reported SE or confirmed inferential unit supports a se_basis other than not_reported (PDF p. 7, Section 4.5.1; PDF p. 9, Section 5.1.2).

The paper states preregistration and names flexibility/originality hypotheses, but does not explicitly call any outcome primary. Primary-outcome status remains not_stated pending the registration. Python urllib requests to the cited AsPredicted URL and the archive.org mirror named in forms/data/c032.json both failed with network socket permission errors; no external document was used.
The retention delay is reported as three weeks, not a number of days. delay_days is null under the instruction not to convert units (PDF p. 6, Section 4.2.4).

The release year and precise deployed ChatGPT-4 model version are not confirmed by the Methods. ai_tool.year is null; the general OpenAI reference is not treated as confirmation of the deployed version (PDF pp. 1, 4-5 and 16, reference [80]).
Individual AUT coder identities and coding reliability are not reported; only detailed scoring is referred to the unavailable supplement (PDF p. 7, Sections 4.5.1-4.5.2).
The retention test is described as unaided, but AI-use prevention/checks and the interim AI-use questionnaire results are not reported (PDF pp. 5-6, Sections 4.2 and 4.2.4).
notes: Extraction B checked the PDF results, all tables, figures, Methods, and references, and read all 105829 characters of the markdown in contiguous chunks. The PDF has no appendix or embedded supplement. All twelve full-sample AUT outcome contrasts are retained, including records whose numerical results are figure-only and therefore null under extraction rule 1. The three contrasts with narrative numerical results are main-test elaboration, immediate post-test fluency, and immediate post-test elaboration. No figure values, standardized effects, derived differences, unit conversions, or inferred p-values are recorded. Originality measures the rarity of individual uses and is coded novelty; no across_people outcome is reported. All phases belong to one between-dyad randomized study, so within_person is null. Shared-sample review: the form identifies no other paper sharing S1; S2 repeats the separately published pre-study in reference [7] and is excluded. Primary status differs from the screening map because preregistered hypotheses alone do not explicitly establish a primary outcome. Quotes with ellipses omit mathematical labels that have corrupt PDF font encodings; every numerical value was checked in page text and the rendered PDF. Extraction date: 2026-10-09.
